# How to Diagnose and Fix Axis Sign and Joint Order Mismatches in Custom Humanoid Re-directions Where One Side is Normal and the Other is Misaligned?

> **Current answer:** The original poster confirmed two issues: the negative direction joint axes in URDF need to be multiplied by -1 at the corresponding DOF positions; the NECK_Y import position disrupts the order of the upper arm joints, requiring adjustment of the order of the worldbody in MuJoCo XML and the ROTATION_AXIS to be in the same order. Only changing the sign of one axis is insufficient to fix the index misalignment. This conclusion was verified on a 30-joint custom humanoid robot and needs re-validation when migrating to other models.

## Key terms

- Joint-axis sign (关节轴符号)
- DOF ordering (自由度顺序)
- Rotation axis table (ROTATION_AXIS) (旋转轴表)
- Forward kinematics (正向运动学)

## Problem and symptoms

- When redirecting a custom humanoid, the left key points align, but the right body is misaligned; how to diagnose the issue?
- Left arm and leg can match the red key points, but the right body cannot; changing a single axis sign does not resolve the issue.

## Environment

- LeCAR-Lab/human2humanoid; stable_punch.pkl; 30-joint custom humanoid; vis_motion.py; MuJoCo XML/URDF; specific submission and version not mentioned.

## Priority diagnostics

- Compare joint axis signs in URDF with runtime ROTATION_AXIS; print the joint order after import to confirm if NECK_Y is inserted before the upper arm DOF and causes index misalignment.

## Possible causes

- Negative-axis joints in URDF are not compensated in dof_pos; NECK_Y is imported before the upper arm DOF, causing the right joint vector to misalign with the ROTATION_AXIS order.

## Attempts

- The questioner first modified the axis sign, but no change occurred; then both the sign matrix of dof_pos and joint order were adjusted.

## Effective fixes

- Create a sign matrix for negative-axis joints in URDF, multiply corresponding dof_pos by -1; adjust the order of NECK_Y in MuJoCo XML worldbody and modify the ROTATION_AXIS in torch_humanoid_batch.py accordingly.

## Result

- The questioner explicitly states the problem resolved and lists the two reasons and fixes mentioned.

## Limitations

- This is a self-test by the author of the custom humanoid; the order of DOF indices by importers (sorted by name, tree structure, or XML order) needs verification in the target toolchain.

## Safety notes

- Incorrect axis signs or joint order can produce commands with opposite directions; verify with small single-joint commands before real machine testing.

## Image and visual evidence

- The original poster used red key points to describe left-right differences, but the root cause and fix are explicitly stated in the questioner's text; no additional conclusions from unreviewed screenshots were added.

## Applicability boundary

- Applies to custom humanoid re-directions where joint axis signs and DOF ordering are explained via separate ROTATION_AXIS tables.
